What differs

  • Proved in sc form, in charts: $T_0O$, $K_0$ (and $T_zO$, $K_z$ in any chart) with the induced sc-structures stand for $T_xX$, $Y_x$, which carry no linear structure here (G.7). Two steps the text leaves out: that $D(g - s)(0) = \Gamma(0)^{-1}Dh(0)D\psi(0)$, the conjugate of the basic germ's linearization, is sc-Fredholm (the criterion of V1.8: $\Gamma(0)$ preserves the levels and $Dh(0)$ is regularizing), and the sc-structures of $T_0O$, $K_0$ (Definition 2.47 at the smooth point $0$, the closed graph theorem). No tameness is assumed. In other charts the levels are transported by the chart change at smooth points (Findings, Chapter 3, items 235, 239). Formerly level $0$ only (G.22, Findings item 48); updated in the third addendum of this page.
  • The first formal statement (proposition_3_52, kept for the theorems that use it) gives the index as “$n - N$ for some $n, N \in \mathbb N$”, which every integer satisfies. proposition_3_52_index names the conjugation data and identifies $n$, $N$ with the dimensions of the conjugating basic germ, for every conjugation (Findings, Chapter 3, item 120). Updated after the first edition of this page.
  • In every other strong bundle chart around $x_0$ the linearization is Fredholm of the same index, and onto at a zero in good position (V3.96). Updated in the second addendum of this page.
  • Germs. The hypothesis is the text’s since the switch to the germ reading (phase 2): an sc-Fredholm germ whose filling and sc$^+$-section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (V3.13); $Dg(0)$ is the value at $0$ of a derivative family of the filling germ, the same for every family on every germ. The forms for germ data on the whole chart are the _wholeChart declarations of the same names (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 289, 310, 331). Hence “restated” (formerly “narrower”, for that hypothesis): what remains is the reading in charts.

Definition 3.53: good position of an sc-Fredholm germ

restated
in the chartno case distinction $d_X \ge 1$sc-complement form: the same at zeros

HWZ §3.6, Definition 3.53, p. 111

An sc-Fredholm germ $(f, x)$ of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ is in good position if (1) $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is surjective and (2) if $d_X(x) \ge 1$, $\ker f'(x)$ is in good position to the partial cone $C_xX$ in $T_xX$.

Proved in Lean

In the chart of Definition 3.11 (IsGoodPositionAtGerm, at $Dg(0)$ for a derivative family $Dg$ of the filling germ $g$): $Tf(0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is onto and $\ker Dg(0)$ is in good position to $C_0O = T_0O \cap C$ inside $T_0O$ (IsInGoodPositionIn); IsGoodPositionAt is the case of a whole-chart filled version. For a section (StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm f x₀): the data of Definition 3.11 at $x_0$ with the germ in good position in that chart. With the text’s sc-complement (IsGoodPositionAtScGerm; for a section StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermSc, in a tame chart): the kernel has a good sc-complement inside $T_0O$ ($T_m = N_m \oplus P_m$ on every level). At a zero of an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data the two forms agree.

The case distinction $d_X(x) \ge 1$ is dropped: at an interior point (2) holds trivially (Findings, Chapter 3, item 50), and for tame germ data good position in a tame chart at a zero with $d_X = 0$ is the surjectivity of the linearization (V3.100).

Updated in the third addendum of this page.
  • Germs. Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the germ data are the text’s (V3.13), and the condition in the chart is read at $Dg(0)$, the value at $0$ of any derivative family of the filling germ (the same for all, IsGoodPositionGerm.forall_isGoodPositionAtGerm); the whole-chart forms are IsGoodPositionGermWholeChart, IsGoodPositionGermScWholeChart (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 280, 320, 330).

Theorem 3.54: the solution set as a graph (part (3) of the proof)

narrower
the graph description (3)tame chart at $x_0$(1), (2): V3.82, V3.85

HWZ §3.6, Theorem 3.54, p. 111 (proof pp. 111–115)

Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle with $f(x) = 0$ and $(f, x)$ in good position. There is an open $V \ni x$ such that $S = \{y \in V \mid f(y) = 0\}$ has: (1) at every $y \in S$, $(f, y)$ is in good position; (2) $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners. The proof shows (3): $\psi\varphi(S) = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V'\}$ for the $\sigma$ of Corollary 3.47 applied to $\Psi_*(g) = h + t$.

Proved in Lean

For a section $f$ of a strong bundle, $f(x_0) = 0$ and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): a tame chart $\varphi$ centred at $x_0$, the conjugating sc-diffeomorphism $\psi$ with its inverse, a basic germ $h' = h + (t_{\mathbb R^N}, 0)$ with the data of Theorem 3.38 and $D(h + t)(0)$ surjective with kernel $K$ in good position, $K$ a smooth subspace; a closed good complement $Y$; $V'$ relatively open in $K \cap C'$, $\sigma : V' \to Y$ $C^1$ with values on level $1$, $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$, every $v + \sigma(v)$ a zero of $h + t$, and $C^k$-lifts $\sigma_k : V_k \to E'_k$ near $0$ for every $k$ (Theorem 3.47 (1)); and an open $V_x \ni x_0$ on which $\psi\varphi$ is injective, $f(y) = 0 \iff (h + t)(\psi\varphi(y)) = 0$, and $\psi\varphi(\{y \in V_x \mid f(y) = 0\}) = \{v + \sigma(v) \mid v \in V'\}$.

Lemma 3.55: good position along a graph

narrower
added: $Y$ closed$\tau$ on all of $N \cap C$ (here)uniform $\gamma$

HWZ §3.6, Lemma 3.55, p. 114 (proof §3.8.3, pp. 132–135)

$C \subseteq E$ a partial quadrant, $N$ a finite-dimensional smooth subspace in good position with good complement $Y$, $V \subseteq N \cap C$ relatively open, $\tau : V \to Y_1$ of class $C^1$ with $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$. Then for $v$ in a relatively open $V' \ni 0$: (1) $v + \tau(v) \in C_1$; (2) $Y$ is a topological complement of $N_v = \{n + D\tau(v)n\}$; (3) there is $\gamma_v > 0$ with $n \in C_x \iff n + y \in C_x$ for $n \in N_v$, $y \in Y$, $|y|_0 \le \gamma_v|n|_0$, $x = v + \tau(v)$.

Proved in Lean

In the model $E = \mathbb R^n \oplus W$, $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ (in coordinates for any $C$ cut out by functionals): for $N$ in good position with closed good complement $Y$ and $\tau : N \to E$ with values in $Y$, $C^1$ on $N \cap C$, $\tau(0) = 0$, $D\tau(0) = 0$: there is $\rho > 0$ such that for $v \in N \cap C$, $|v| < \rho$: $v + \tau(v) \in C$ and $Y$ is a good complement of $N_v$ with respect to $C_{v + \tau(v)}$ (so $E_0 = N_v \oplus Y$, both closed), with a constant independent of $v$.

Theorem 3.56: the global implicit function theorem, $\partial X = \emptyset$ (from the tangent germ property)

narrower
assumes the tangent germ property of $S$

HWZ §3.6, Theorem 3.56, p. 115

If $P : Y \to X$ is a tame strong bundle over an M-polyfold with $\partial X = \emptyset$ and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with surjective linearization at every point of $S = \{f = 0\}$, then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold without boundary.

Proved in Lean

If $X$ is without boundary and $S = \{f = 0\} \ne \emptyset$ has at every point the regular data of Definition 3.25 (V3.22, IsRegular), then $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is that of an $n$-dimensional manifold with corners and is without boundary.

Theorem 3.19: the implicit function theorem, interior case (first form)

narrower

HWZ §3.1, Theorem 3.19, p. 74

Let $X$ be an M-polyfold with $d_X \equiv 0$, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section of a strong bundle and $f(x_0) = 0$. Then $f'(x_0) : T_{x_0}X \to Y_{x_0}$ is sc-Fredholm. If it is surjective, there is an open $U \ni x_0$ such that $S(f, U) = \{y \in U \mid f(y) = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is that of a smooth manifold of dimension the Fredholm index, $f'(y)$ is surjective at every $y \in S(f, U)$, and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$.

Proved in Lean

Let $d_X \equiv 0$, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart with a filler satisfying condition (3) of Definition 3.4 at its zeros near $0$ (IsGoodPositionGermFilled, V3.82). Then there are an open $U \ni x_0$ and $d \in \mathbb N$ such that every zero in $U$ is a smooth point with $(f, y)$ in good position in a tame chart, and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners with degeneracy index $0$ everywhere. First clause: in the chart at $x_0$, $Dg(0)$ and $f'(x_0) = Tf(x_0) : T_0O \to K_0$ are sc-Fredholm operators and $Tf(x_0)$ is onto on every level (Proposition 3.52, V3.46); in every strong bundle chart around $x_0$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm with the same index on every level (StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm, V3.96).

HWZ §3.1, Theorem 3.23, p. 77

Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle, $f(x) = 0$, $f'(x)$ surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$. HWZ §3.1, Corollary 3.24, p. 78

If at every zero $x$ of the sc-Fredholm section $f$ of a tame strong bundle $f'(x)$ is surjective with kernel in good position to $C_xX$, then the solution set $S = \{f = 0\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and that of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

Proved in Lean

The same with good position in the text's sense (sc-complement, V3.47) at every zero, which for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data is the same hypothesis (corollary_3_24_sc).

Tameness is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms and by open subsets

not in the book
used silently by the text

HWZ §3.2, proof of Proposition 3.26, p. 80; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 114

Used without statement: in the proof of Proposition 3.26, “$X' = \psi(X)$ is tame”; in the proof of Theorem 3.54, the chart $\psi \circ \varphi$ onto $\psi(O)$ is a chart of the tame M-polyfold $X$.

Proved in Lean

For an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi : U \to U'$ between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants and a tame retraction $r : U \to U$ onto $O$, $\psi \circ r \circ \psi^{-1}$ is a tame retraction of $U'$ onto $\psi(O)$, so $(\psi(O), C', E')$ is a tame retract; on the way $d_{C'} \circ \psi = d_C$, $Dr'(\psi(x)) = D\psi(x)Dr(x)D\psi^{-1}(\psi(x))$, and sc-isomorphisms carry sc-subspaces and sc-splittings. The restriction of a tame retraction to an open subset is tame; an open subset of a tame retract, and the model of a chart restricted to an open set, are tame retracts.

HWZ §3.4, Corollary 3.39, p. 93

If the sc-germ $g$ is equivalent by a strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi$ to a basic germ and $s$ is an sc$^+$-germ, there is a strong bundle map $\Psi$ such that $((\Psi \circ \Phi)_*(g + s))^1$ is a basic germ.

With $t = \Phi[1]_*s$ and $h' = h + (t_{\mathbb R^N}, 0)$ there are data of Theorem 3.38 for $t_W$ such that $\Phi_*(g + s) = h + t$ near $0$, $\Gamma = \Lambda \circ \Phi^1$ is a strong bundle isomorphism of the shifted structures $E^1 \triangleleft F^1$ with $\Gamma_* = \Lambda_* \circ \Phi^1_*$, and $(\Gamma(u, (g + s)^1(u)))_2 = (\Lambda_*(h + t))^1(\gamma(u))$ near $0$, a basic germ; so $(g + s)^1$ is conjugated to a basic germ. Also $\Gamma = (\Lambda_0 \circ \Phi)^1$.

HWZ §3.5, Theorem 3.43 and Corollary 3.47, pp. 102, 106; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 114

Theorem 3.43 and Corollary 3.47 (local solvability) with a good complement $Y$ of the kernel; Theorem 3.54, step (3): the solution set near $x$ is the graph of $\sigma$ over $\ker D(h + t)(0) \cap C'$.

Proved in Lean

The conclusions of V3.38, V3.42 and V3.48 hold with a good complement $Y$ that is closed and satisfies ProjectsInto for the partial quadrant (V3.75). In Theorem 3.43, $Y = Z \oplus W$ for a good complement $Z$ of $\widetilde K$ chosen by V3.75: every good complement $Z$ of $\widetilde K$ gives the good complement $Z \oplus W$ of $K'$ (constant $\varepsilon/(\|L\| + 1)$) and the data of the proof exist for a prescribed $Z$; in Corollary 3.47 both properties are carried by the linear homeomorphism of Theorem 3.38.

  • Two additional conclusions. V3.78

The linearization at a zero in charts, and its chart independence

not in the book
presupposed by the textat zeros onlytransition smooth on $[0]$ only

HWZ §3.6, Definition 3.53, p. 111; §2.4, Definition 2.38, p. 42

Definition 3.53 is stated with $f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ and the partial cone $C_xX$; Definition 2.38 asserts that $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ do not depend on the chart (Proposition 2.30). The linearization is defined at the centre of a chart, through a filler.

Proved in Lean

In a strong bundle chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) = D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)|_{T_zO}$ at every level-$1$ point $z$ of the retract; at a zero it takes values in $K_z = \rho(z)F$ and equals $Dg(z)$ on $T_zO$ for every $g$ sc$^1$ on $U$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$, and for every sc$^1$-germ $g$ agreeing with $\mathbf f$ near $z$ with $z$ in its germ, $Dg(z)$ the value of its derivative family (linAt_eq_germDeriv; at a centre: $Tf(0)$ of Proposition 3.5, also for a filling germ). For two strong bundle charts of $P$ and an sc-smooth section, at a zero $y$ with level-$1$ points $z$, $z'$ over $\varphi(y)$, $\varphi'(y)$: isomorphisms $A : T_zO \to T_{z'}O'$, $\Gamma : K_z \to K'_{z'}$ with $\Gamma\,\mathrm{Lin}(z) = \mathrm{Lin}'(z')A$ and $A$ respecting the partial quadrants; so surjectivity, the Fredholm property and index, and the good position of the kernel do not depend on the chart.

What differs

  • The text does not prove the chart independence of $f'(x)$ or of good position; this is its chart form at zeros (what gap G.13 of Chapter 2 leaves open). Only the fibre derivative of the transition survives at a zero, so away from zeros the linearization is not chart independent. Of Definition 2.50 only the sc-smoothness of the transition on $[0]$ is used; level-$1$ points suffice; no tameness (Findings, Chapter 3, items 110–116). Added after the first edition of this page.
  • For filling germs (the germ reading of Definition 3.11) $Dg(z)$ is meaningful only for $z$ in the germ; the consumers use it at the centre and at the level-$1$ lifts of nearby zeros, which lie in the germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 278, 284). Definition 3.53 at a zero, from a chart not centred there

not in the book
dense range sufficeskernel: $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$

HWZ §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 115

In the proof of Theorem 3.54: at every zero $y$ near $x$, $f'(y)$ is surjective with kernel in good position, “so that, proceeding as above”, the construction can be repeated at $y$.

Proved in Lean

Let $f$ be an sc-smooth section, $y$ a zero with tame germ data (V3.103), $c$ a strong bundle chart of $P$ around $y$ (not necessarily centred), $z$ a level-$1$ point over $\varphi(y)$, $g$ an sc$^1$-germ on a germ $G$ of $c$ with derivative family $Dg$ and $z \in G_1$, agreeing with $\mathbf f$ on $O$ near $\varphi(y)$. If $\rho(z)k \in Dg(z)(T_zO)$ for every smooth $k$ and $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$ is in good position to $C_{\varphi(y)}$ inside $T_zO$, then $(f, y)$ is in good position in a tame chart (isGoodPositionGermTame_of_chart_dense); with all of $K_z$ in the range, for an sc-Fredholm germ, in the chart of Definition 3.11 (isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart); the same with the hypotheses on $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ (isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj).

What differs

  • The hypothesis is on $\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO$, not on $\ker Dg(z)$: condition (3) of the filler holds at its centre only, so $\ker Dg(z)$ need not lie in $T_zO$. A dense part of $K_z$ in the range suffices because the range of the linearization in the centred chart is closed (Proposition 3.52) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 111, 117). Added after the first edition of this page.
  • In the germ reading of Definition 3.11 the point $z$ must lie in the germ of $g$; the dense form needs the closed range in the target chart, which Proposition 3.52 for germs gives in the tame chart of the germ data, so it is stated there. The whole-chart forms are isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart_dense, isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt and the _wholeChart declarations (Findings, Chapter 3, items 285, 301, 313). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.11 to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

HWZ §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, property (4), and Lemma 3.55, p. 114

For every zero $y \in V$, with $\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)$, the kernel of $f'(y)$ is in good position and $f'(y)$ is surjective; this follows from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55.

Proved in Lean

In the data of V3.48 (a section, $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart) there are a presentation $T$ of $C'$ and an open $V_{x,1} \ni x_0$ such that for every zero $y \in V_{x,1}$ with $\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)$: $v + \sigma(v)$ lies on level $1$ and $D(h + t)$ there is surjective Fredholm of index $n - N$; $v + \sigma(v) \in C'$; and $Y$ is a good complement of $N_v = \{k + D\sigma(v)k\}$ with respect to $C'_{v + \sigma(v)}$, with $N_v$ in good position. Lemma 3.55 for $\sigma$ on a relatively open $V \subseteq N \cap C$, any presentation of $C$, closed $Y$.

HWZ §3.6, Theorem 3.54 (1), the kernel, pp. 111, 114

At every zero $y$ near $x$, $\ker f'(y)$ is in good position to the partial cone $C_yX$ (from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55).

Proved in Lean

For a section $f$ of a strong bundle, $f(x_0) = 0$ and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): in a tame chart centred at $x_0$ (filling germ $g$ with a derivative family $Dg$, conjugation covering $\psi$, the germ $h + t$ with kernel $K$, graph $\sigma$) there is an open $V_{x,2} \ni x_0$ such that at every zero $y \in V_{x,2}$, $z_0 = \varphi(y)$, whose level-$1$ lift lies in the germ of $g$: $N_v = \ker D(h + t)$ at $v + \sigma(v) = \psi(z_0)$; $\ker Dg(z_0) = D\psi^{-1}(N_v)$; $Dg(z_0)$ is onto; $\ker Dg(z_0) \subseteq T_{z_0}O$; and $\ker Dg(z_0)$ is in good position to $C_{z_0}$ inside $T_{z_0}O$.

What differs

  • The kernel half of (1), in the chart at $x_0$, with the text's hypotheses. Two steps the text does not mention: $N_v \subseteq \ker D(h + t)$ needs the $C^1$-lift of $\sigma$ into level $1$ (Theorem 3.47 (1)), equality follows from a dimension count; and $\ker Dg(z_0) \subseteq T_{z_0}O$ comes from the tangency of the solution set to $O$, not from the filler, whose condition (3) holds at $0$ only (Findings, Chapter 3, items 101–104). The surjectivity half is V3.93. Added after the first edition of this page.
  • Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (htame), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).
  • In the germ reading the level-$1$ lift of $z_0$ lies in the germ of the filling because the basic germ is taken on the points that $\psi^{-1}$ maps into the germs of $g$ and $s$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 276–278, 295). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.11 to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

HWZ §3.6, Theorem 3.54 (1), p. 111 (proof p. 114)

At every zero $y$ near $x$, the sc-Fredholm germ $(f, y)$ is in good position: $f'(y)$ is surjective and its kernel is in good position (from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55).

Proved in Lean

Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, and $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart with a filler $g$ that satisfies condition (3) of Definition 3.4 at its zeros near $0$ (IsGoodPositionGermFilled: at every level-$1$ zero $z_1$ of $g$ in $O \cap N$ lying in the germ of $g$, for its derivative family $Dg$, $Dr(z_1)b = 0$ and $\rho(z_1)Dg(z_1)b = Dg(z_1)b$ imply $b = 0$). Then there is an open $V_x \ni x_0$ such that $(f, y)$ is in good position in a tame chart at every zero $y \in V_x$. Step: at a zero $z$ with $Dg(z)$ onto and condition (3) at $z$, $\rho(z)F \subseteq Dg(z)(T_zO)$.

Theorem 3.18: parametrized perturbations

stronger
no tameness“readily verified”: provedtranslation charts of $\mathbb R^n$

HWZ §3.1, Theorem 3.18, p. 74

Let $P : Y \to X$ be a tame strong bundle and $f$ an sc-Fredholm section. If $s_1, \dots, s_n \in \Gamma^+(P)$, then $(r, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)$ defines an sc-Fredholm section of the pull-back bundle $\pi^*(P) : \pi^*Y \to \mathbb R^n \times X$.

The paracompactness of $\mathbb R^n \times X$ and $\pi^*Y$ is supplied by Theorem 2.16 (theorem_3_18'). On the way: $\tilde f = f \circ \pi$ is sc-Fredholm (product chart, the $\mathbb R^n$-extension of the basic germ), $\tilde s$ is sc$^+$ (scalar product rule), $F = \tilde f + \tilde s$, Theorem 3.15; $\mathbb R^n \times X$ is tame when $X$ is.

What differs

At $(r_0, x)$ with $r_0 \ne 0$ the first term is the linearization of $f + \sum r_{0,i}s_i$, not $f'(x)$; the formula does not use $F(r_0, x) = 0$. Theorem 3.54 (1): the surjectivity at the nearby zeros, in the chart at $x_0$

not in the book
a new argument$N_4$ independent of $k$no added hypothesis

HWZ §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, property (4), p. 114

For every zero $y$ near $x$ the linearization $f'(y)$ is surjective; “property (4) follows from Corollary 3.41 and from Lemma 3.55”.

Proved in Lean

In the data of V3.48 at a zero $x_0$ in good position (chart centred at $x_0$, filling germ $g$, conjugation $\Psi$ covering $\psi$, $h' + \iota t$ with kernel $K \ne 0$, the graph $\sigma$ over $V'$, an open $N_2 \ni 0$ on which $\psi$ maps the zeros of $g$ in $O$ onto the graph), with condition (2) of Definition 3.4 on $N_2$: there is an open $N_4 \subseteq N_2$ containing $0$ such that for every zero $z_0 \in O \cap N_4$ of $g$ and every smooth $k$, $\rho(z_0)k = Dg(z_0)x$ for some $x \in T_{z_0}O$. The curve $u(\mu)$ of zeros of $g + \mu\rho(r(\cdot))k$ through $z_0$ lies in $O$ (condition (2)) and in the germ of $g$; it comes from Theorem 3.30 at the centre for the $k$-extended contraction germ of the normal form of Theorem 3.38, whose regions in $a$ do not depend on $k$, and from a one-sided finite-dimensional implicit function theorem at $\theta(z_0)$ along an inward direction given by good position.

What differs

  • Not the text's argument, which gives the surjectivity of the filled $Dg(z_0)$ only (V3.82). The perturbation argument of the text's Proposition 6.2 applies the implicit function theorem at $x_0$ to a problem depending on the perturbation, with a neighbourhood depending on it (V3.83); here the finite-dimensional implicit function theorem is applied at the nearby zero, and Theorem 3.30 at the centre to a germ whose $a$-regions are $k$-independent, so $N_4$ is determined by $g$, $r$, $\rho$, $\Psi$ and the normal form. The surjectivity of $D_aH$ at the nearby zero comes from a dimension count on level $0$, not from eliminating the $W$-block; Corollary 3.39 is not used (Findings, Chapter 3, items 180–187). Added in the second addendum of this page.
  • In the germ reading the curve lies in the germ of the filling: its points come from the germ of the basic germ taken on the points that $\psi^{-1}$ maps into the germs of $g$ and $s$, so $g$ is differentiated within its germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 276–278, 298). Updated after the switch of Definition 3.11 to the text’s germ reading (phase 2).

Theorem 3.54 (1)–(2) with the text's hypotheses

restated
the text's hypotheses(2) as regular dataproof of (1): V3.93repaired: tame charts (V3.103)conclusion with the sc-complement

HWZ §3.6, Theorem 3.54 (1), (2), p. 111

Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle, $f(x) = 0$, $(f, x)$ in good position. There is an open $V \ni x$ such that $S = \{y \in V \mid f(y) = 0\}$ satisfies: (1) $(f, y)$ is in good position at every $y \in S$; (2) $S$ is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is equivalent to a smooth manifold with boundary with corners.

Proved in Lean

For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart: an open $V_x \ni x_0$ such that $(f, y)$ is in good position in a tame chart at every zero $y \in V_x$ (theorem_3_54_one'), and $d$ with regular data of Definition 3.25 of dimension $d$ for $S$ at $x_0$ with chart domain in $V_x$, every datum at a point of $S$ in that domain having dimension $d$ (theorem_3_54'). With the text's notion of good position (sc-complement, V3.47) in the conclusion, from either form at $x_0$: every zero $y \in V_x$ is in good position with an sc-complement (theorem_3_54_one_sc_of_tame, theorem_3_54_one_sc; with (2), theorem_3_54_sc).

HWZ §3.1, Theorems 3.19, 3.23, pp. 74, 77

(3.23) For an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle and a zero $x$ with $f'(x)$ onto and kernel in good position to $C_xX$, there is an open $U \ni x$ such that $S(f, U)$ consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold with a uniquely determined structure of a manifold with boundary with corners. (3.19) For $d_X \equiv 0$ and $f'(x_0)$ onto, $S(f, U)$ is a smooth manifold.

Proved in Lean

For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x) = 0$, $(f, x)$ in good position in a tame chart: an open $U \ni x$ and $d$ such that every zero in $U$ is in good position in a tame chart and a smooth point, and $S(f, U)$ is a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners (theorem_3_23'); if $d_X \equiv 0$, with degeneracy index $0$ everywhere (theorem_3_19'). Theorem 3.23 with the text's notion of good position (sc-complement, V3.47) at $x$ and, in the conclusion, at every zero in $U$: theorem_3_23_sc.

V3.96

The index of the linearization at a zero, in every chart

stronger
sc-Fredholm on every level, in chartsevery chart, at every zero

HWZ §3.6, Proposition 3.52, p. 110; Theorem 3.19, p. 74

If $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section and $f(x) = 0$, then $Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x$ is an sc-Fredholm operator (Proposition 3.52); “the linearization $f'(x_0)$ is a sc-Fredholm operator” (Theorem 3.19).

Proved in Lean

IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d: in every strong bundle chart around $y$, at the level-$1$ point over $\varphi(y)$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is onto, Fredholm, $\mathrm{ind} = \dim\ker = d$. For an sc-smooth section and the chart of Definition 3.11 at a zero $x_0$ with conjugation data of $g - s$ to a basic germ $O(\widetilde C \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$, $\widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$: in every chart around $x_0$ the linearization is Fredholm of index $n - N$, onto if the germ is in good position; so IsSurjLinOfIndex f x_0 (n − N) at a zero in good position. For an sc-Fredholm section in good position, in the chart of Definition 3.53: $\mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0) = \mathrm{ind}\,Tf(x_0) = \dim\ker Tf(x_0) = n - N$ for every conjugation. In sc form: for an sc-Fredholm section, a zero $y$ and any strong bundle chart around $y$, at the level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(y)$ (a smooth point), $T_zO = Dr(z)E$ and $K_z = \rho(z)F$ are sc-subspaces and $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is an sc-Fredholm operator, Fredholm on every level of the index $n - N$ of every conjugation of every germ datum at $y$; under IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d it is onto on every level, of index $d$ on every level. In the chart of Definition 3.53 at a zero in good position, $Dg(0)$ and $f'(x_0) = Tf(x_0)$ are sc-Fredholm and $Tf(x_0)$ is onto on every level.

What differs

  • Proved in sc form, in every chart: the level-$0$ conjugation between the linearizations in two charts (V3.78) is realised by bounded operators on the ambient spaces that preserve the levels at smooth points (derivatives of the sc-smooth transition maps, and the fibre part of the strong bundle transition, sc$^0$ on $Y[0]$), so the regularity of the linearization in the chart of the germ (V3.46) passes to every chart; then the criterion of V1.8. Tameness is not used. $T_xX$ itself carries no linear structure here (G.7), so the operator is read in charts. The passage to every chart is the chart independence at zeros, which the text does not state (Findings, Chapter 3, items 170, 236, 239). Added in the second addendum of this page with the level-$0$ Fredholm property only (G.22); updated in the third addendum.
  • Germs. The hypothesis is the text’s since the switch to the germ reading (phase 2): the germ data of the sc-Fredholm section are germs whose levels may shrink with $m$ (V3.13, V3.16), and Proposition 3.52 enters at the centre of the chart of the germ datum, where $\mathrm{Lin}(0) = Dg(0)$ on $T_0O$ for the filling germ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 284, 310, 314, 330). theorem_3_19_linearization_sc gives the conclusions in the chart at $x_0$, and linAt_isScFredholm_of_isSurjLinOfIndex with IsGoodPositionGerm.exists_isSurjLinOfIndex in every chart. Hence “stronger” (formerly “narrower”, for the hypothesis): the index on every level, and the surjectivity on every level at a zero in good position, in every chart, go beyond the text’s statement.
V3.97

The dimension of the solution set is the Fredholm index

stronger
at every zero, in every chartalso Theorems 3.23, 3.57repaired: tame charts (V3.103)

HWZ §3.1, Theorem 3.19, p. 74; §3.6, proof of Theorem 3.54, p. 115

The solution set $S(f, U)$ has the structure of a smooth manifold “whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index” (Theorem 3.19); with $d = \dim\ker f'(x)$ the solution set has the $d$-dimensional tangent germ property (proof of Theorem 3.54).

Proved in Lean

For an sc-smooth section and a zero $x_0$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): the data of Definition 3.25 at $x_0$ have a dimension $d$ with IsSurjLinOfIndex f x_0 d, also the regular data of Theorem 3.54 (2). For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data: an open $U \ni x_0$ and $d$ with every zero $y \in U$ in good position in a tame chart, IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d, and $S(f, U)$ a tame $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners (theorem_3_23_index; without boundary if $d_X \equiv 0$, theorem_3_19_index); under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.57, regular data at every zero whose dimension is the index at the zeros of their chart domain (theorem_3_57_index). For an sc-Fredholm section, at a zero $y$ with IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d, in every chart $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is moreover sc-Fredholm and onto on every level, of index $d$ on every level.

What differs

  • $d = \dim\ker D(h + t)(0) = n - N$ for the conjugation from which the chart of the tangent germ data is built, and $n - N$ is the index of $f'(x_0)$ for the same conjugation (Proposition 3.52); the proofs of Theorem 3.54 had to expose that conjugation (_conj forms). The index is stated at every zero near the point and in every chart; the text states no dimension in Theorems 3.23 and 3.57 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 170). Added in the second addendum of this page.
  • Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (htame), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).
  • That $d$ is the index on every level of $f'(y)$ as an sc-Fredholm operator, in every chart, is V3.96 (Findings, Chapter 3, item 239). Updated in the third addendum of this page.
V3.98

The Fredholm index along the solution set and along paths (Definition 6.1, Proposition 6.2)

narrower
paths on $\mathbb R$Definition 6.1 local sectionDefinition 6.1 well defined, no Prop. 1.10repaired: tame charts (V3.103)sc-index, every level, every chart

HWZ Definition 6.1, pp. 200–201; Proposition 6.2, p. 201

Definition 6.1: at a smooth point $x$, $\mathrm{ind}(f, x)$ is the Fredholm index of $(f - s)'(x)$ for a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(x) = f(x)$; it does not depend on $s$. Proposition 6.2: over a tame M-polyfold, if $x_0$, $x_1$ are smooth points connected by an sc-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to X$, then $\mathrm{ind}(f, x_0) = \mathrm{ind}(f, x_1)$. In Chapter 3 the statement along the solution set is implicit in Theorem 3.54 (1).

Proved in Lean

For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103), $f(x_0) = 0$, $(f, x_0)$ in good position in a tame chart: an open $V_x \ni x_0$ and $d$ with IsSurjLinOfIndex f y d at every zero $y \in V_x$, so $\mathrm{ind}\,f'(y) = \dim\ker f'(y) = \mathrm{ind}\,f'(x_0)$. With Theorem 3.54: every zero in $V_x$ in good position in a tame chart, and regular data of dimension $d$ at $x_0$ with chart domain $V_x$. In sc form: at every zero $y \in V_x$, in every strong bundle chart around $y$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, onto on every level and of index $d$ on every level; at any zero of an sc-Fredholm section, in every chart, $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm with the same index on every level (StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm). Without good position, with the text’s hypotheses: if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and $f(x_0) = 0$, there are an open $V \ni x_0$ and $i \in \mathbb Z$ such that at every zero $y \in V$, in every strong bundle chart around $y$, $f'(y)$ is Fredholm of index $i$ (IsLinOfIndex; index_locally_constant_tame), and in sc form $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm of index $i$ on every level (theorem_3_54_index_locally_constant_general_tame); neither good position, nor surjectivity at $x_0$, nor bump functions are assumed (the first forms, for $X$ admitting sc-smooth bump functions (Definition 5.9): index_locally_constant_of_admitsBumpFunctions, theorem_3_54_index_locally_constant_general). Definition 6.1 (StrongBundle.IsIndexAtLocal f x i, with the text’s locally defined section): there are an open $V \ni x$ and an sc$^+$-section $s$ of the restriction $P|V$ (StrongBundle.restrictOpen) with $(f|_V + s)(x) = 0$ and $(f|_V + s)'(x)$ Fredholm of index $i$ in every strong bundle chart of $P|V$; for an sc-Fredholm section the index is unique (IsIndexAtLocal.unique), at a zero it is the index of $f'(x)$, and it exists at every smooth point (exists_isIndexAtLocal). The reading with an sc$^+$-section on all of $X$ (StrongBundle.IsIndexAt; unique, IsIndexAt.unique; existing at every smooth point if $X$ admits bump functions, exists_isIndexAt) implies it, and is the same notion when $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions (isIndexAtLocal_iff_isIndexAt). Proposition 6.2 (proposition_6_2_local): if $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data, then for every sc-smooth path $\varphi : \mathbb R \to X$ there is $i$ with $\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t)) = i$ for all $t$, and any two values of the index at $\varphi(0)$ and $\varphi(1)$ agree (proposition_6_2_local'); if $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions, the same holds for the global reading (proposition_6_2).

What differs

  • Proposition 6.2 is proved with the text’s hypotheses (fifth addendum of this page; in the fourth, with bump functions), by the text’s device run on the restriction $P|V$ of $P$ to the domain $V$ of a strong bundle chart around $\varphi(t_0)$ (StrongBundle.restrictOpen), for each $t_0$: an sc$^+$-section $S$ of the pull-back to $\mathbb R \times V$ with $\tilde f + S = 0$ along the graph of the path near $t_0$ (the text’s $s(t, x) = R(x, f(\varphi(t)))$ in the chart, with no cut-off, since the chart covers $V$), the local constancy of the index of $\tilde f + S$ along its zero set (stabilizing sections $R(\cdot, e_i)$ in the product chart, again without cut-off, and the implicit function theorem), the index count $\mathrm{ind}(\tilde f + S)'(t, x) = \mathrm{ind}(f, x) + 1$ through the slice $S(t, \cdot)$ (isIndexAt_of_pullback_isLinOfIndex), and the connectedness of $\mathbb R$ (proposition_6_2_local). No bump functions are assumed (“we do not need a sc-smooth partition of unity”, p. 202); tame germ data are the project’s reading of the text’s tameness (V3.103), as in V3.94, where they are no narrowing. With bump functions the proposition holds for the global reading of Definition 6.1 as well (proposition_6_2, the form of the fourth addendum, whose section along the path is cut off by a bump; exists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_path) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 340–349, 360–367).
  • Why still “narrower”. The path is $\varphi : \mathbb R \to X$, not $[0, 1] \to X$: $\mathbb R \times X$ is the product of Theorem 3.18 and has no boundary, and the text’s tame M-polyfold $[0, 1] \times X$ is not used. A path on $[0, 1]$ that extends sc-smoothly to $\mathbb R$ is covered; a path sc-smooth on $[0, 1]$ only, in the sense of M-polyfolds with boundary, is not, and the project has no M-polyfold $[0, 1]$. This is the one narrowing left: the bump functions are gone, Definition 6.1 has the text’s local sections, and the hypotheses on $f$ are the text’s in the project’s reading of tameness.
  • Definition 6.1 has no row of its own. It is IsIndexAtLocal: the text’s locally defined sc$^+$-section is a section of the restriction $P|V$ to an open $V \ni x$ — the restriction of a strong bundle to an open set, which the text uses without comment, is constructed (StrongBundle.restrictOpen, whose atlas consists of the charts of $P$ inside $V$) — and the text’s $f - s$, $s(x) = f(x)$, is written $f + s$, $(f + s)(x) = 0$. It is well defined, two local sections being compared on the intersection of their domains (IsIndexAtLocal.unique), and it exists at every smooth point without bump functions, through the section $-R(\cdot, f(x))$ on a chart domain (exists_isIndexAtLocal). The global reading IsIndexAt of the fourth addendum implies it, and when $X$ admits bump functions the two agree, the local section being cut off (isIndexAtLocal_iff_isIndexAt). The independence of $s$ is proved from the germ data and Theorem 3.15, without the text’s appeal to Proposition 1.10, for which the project has no lemma that the linearization of an sc$^+$-section is compact (Findings, Chapter 3, items 340, 364, 367).
  • Along the solution set the formal proof combines the good position of the nearby zeros (V3.94), the local constancy of the dimension (V3.85) and dimension = index at each zero (V3.97); the text’s proof of Proposition 6.2 uses the step of V3.82 for an extended section, which along solution sets is repaired by V3.93 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 171, 188). Added in the second addendum of this page.
  • Updated after the repair of the tameness hypothesis: first proved with “the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame” (htame), which no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies (V3.104), so that form was vacuous; now with the hypotheses of V3.103 (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192).
  • The sc form (the index of $f'(y)$ as an sc-Fredholm operator, on every level, in every chart) is proved as well; that $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is sc-Fredholm at every zero in every chart, with the level-$0$ index on every level, is StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm (V3.96), cited here since the fifth addendum. The local constancy without good position holds with the text’s hypotheses (tame germ data, no bump functions; index_locally_constant_tame, in sc form theorem_3_54_index_locally_constant_general_tame), by the text’s device for Proposition 6.2 on the restriction $P|V$ to a chart domain: finitely many sc$^+$-sections $R(\cdot, e_i)$, which on $P|V$ need no cut-off, put the parametrized section of Theorem 3.18 into general position at $(0, x_0)$, its index is constant along its solution set (the case above), at $(0, y)$ it is $k + \operatorname{ind} f'(y)$, and the index at a zero is the same for $P$ and $P|V$, through the germ datum (Findings, Chapter 3, items 240–242, 360–363). The first proof, for M-polyfolds admitting bump functions (Lemma 5.11 for the sections), is kept (index_locally_constant_of_admitsBumpFunctions). The candidate counterexample of items 188 and 243 is excluded under tame germ data by Theorem 3.54 (1). Without tame germ data the question is open: $\operatorname{ind} f'(y) = \operatorname{ind} f'(x_0)$ iff the block $C(z) = (1 - \rho(z))Dg(z)|_{\ker Dr(z)}$ of the filling has index $0$, which condition (3) of Definition 3.4 gives at $z = 0$ only (items 243, 343). Updated in the third, fourth and fifth addenda of this page.
V3.99

$\ker f'(y) = T_yS$ in a chart

restated
in the chart $\psi\varphi$$T_yS \subseteq T_yX$: G.13repaired: tame charts (V3.103)

HWZ §3.1, Theorem 3.19, p. 74

$U$ can be chosen such that for $y \in S(f, U)$ the linearization $f'(y)$ is surjective and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$ is the tangent space.

Proved in Lean

For an sc-smooth section and a zero $x_0$ in good position in a tame chart (V3.103): in a tame chart $c$ centred at $x_0$ (as in Definition 3.53), with the conjugating sc-diffeomorphism $\psi$, $K = \ker D(h + t)(0)$ and the solution graph $\sigma : V' \to E'$ ($C^1$, $\sigma(0) = 0$, $D\sigma(0) = 0$) with $\psi\varphi(\{y \in V_x \mid f(y) = 0\}) = \{v + \sigma(v)\}$, there is an open $V_{x,2} \ni x_0$ such that at every zero $y \in V_{x,2}$ with $\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)$ and every level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(y)$, $D\psi(z)$ maps $\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ onto $N_v = \{n + D\sigma(v)n \mid n \in K\}$.

(b) If moreover $Dg(z)$ is onto and $g$ fills $\mathbf f$ near $z_0$ with $\mathbf f(z_0) = 0$, the two conditions are equivalent. (c) For an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (V3.103) and a zero $x_0$ in good position in a tame chart, IsGoodPositionGermFilled f x_0 holds (in a tame chart).

Definitions 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53 in a tame chart

hypotheses explicit
the hypotheses of §3.6tame chart of the germ datasatisfiablefiller chart-bound

HWZ §3.6, Definitions 3.50, 3.51, p. 110; Definition 3.53, p. 111

(3.50) For an sc-smooth section $f$ of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and a smooth point $x$: $(f, x)$ is an sc-Fredholm germ if there is a strong bundle chart $\Phi : \Phi^{-1}(V) \to K$ around $x$ covering $\varphi : (V, x) \to (O, 0)$, “where $K \to O$ is a tame strong local bundle”, in which the local section has a filling $g$ near $0$ and a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(0) = g(0)$ and $g - s$ conjugated near $0$ to a basic germ. (3.51) An sc-smooth section of the tame strong bundle is sc-Fredholm if it is regularizing and an sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point. (3.53) Good position is defined for an sc-Fredholm germ of a tame strong bundle. A strong bundle retraction is tame when its base retraction $r$ is (p. 49).

Proved in Lean

StrongBundle.IsTameChart: a strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas whose base retraction $r : U \to U$ is tame (Definition 2.34). IsScFredholmGermTame f x (“tame germ data”): $x$ smooth and the data of Definition 3.11 in the text’s germ reading (V3.13) in a tame chart. IsGoodPositionGermTame f x: the same data with the germ in good position in that chart (V3.47). IsScFredholmSectionTame f: an sc-Fredholm section (V3.16) with tame germ data at every smooth point. Each implies the form without tameness; good position in a tame chart gives tame germ data; IsGoodPositionGermFilled (V3.82) is stated in a tame chart. A retraction agreeing on its domain with a tame one is tame, so a compatible chart whose base retraction is the identity of $U$ is tame.

  • These are the hypotheses of the implicit function theorems of §3.6 (V3.48, V3.68–V3.70, V3.80–V3.82, V3.84–V3.87, V3.94–V3.102). They were first proved with “tame strong bundle” read as: the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame. No strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies that (V3.104), so those first statements were vacuous; the proofs used the tameness only for particular charts, and the repair changed the statements, not the arguments (Findings, Chapter 3, items 190–192, 198).
  • Whether germ data in some chart (V3.13) can be moved to some compatible tame chart when the atlas consists of tame charts (Definition 3.11 $\Rightarrow$ Definition 3.50) is open. It cannot be done by re-centring a chart of the tame atlas: whether a filling exists in a chart depends on the chart ($\ker Dr(0) \cong \ker\rho(0)$ is necessary, IsFillingGerm.nonempty_kerEquiv), and the trivial bundle with the one-chart tame atlas of evenBundleChart has sc-Fredholm sections with tame germ data in compatible charts but none in the atlas chart (tame_atlas_no_germData_in_atlas_chart). The text builds the tame chart into Definition 3.50, and so do the theorems (Findings, Chapter 3, items 199, 350–353). Updated in the fourth addendum of this page.
  • Germs. Since the switch to the text’s germ reading (phase 2) the three notions carry the germ data of the text (V3.13, V3.45); the earlier whole-chart forms are IsScFredholmGermTameWholeChart, IsGoodPositionGermTameWholeChart, IsScFredholmSectionTameWholeChart, and the non-vacuity witnesses satisfy both readings (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 304, 330). V3.104

A non-tame retraction onto a product with a point: the earlier tameness hypothesis cannot be met

not in the book
the vacuity, retraction-level halfchart-level half not formalized

HWZ no counterpart in the text (Definitions 2.34, 2.50, pp. 39–40, 51–52)

Not in the text. Definition 2.34 (1) asks a tame retraction to preserve the degeneracy index, $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$; Definition 2.50 asks of compatible strong bundle charts only that their transition maps be sc-smooth.

Proved in Lean

For an sc-Banach space $W$, the constant retraction $c : (a, w) \mapsto (1, 0)$ of the partial quadrant $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ of $\mathbb R \oplus W$ (sc-smooth, with retract $\{(1, 0)\}$), and every sc-smooth retraction $r$ of a nonempty relatively open $U$ in a partial quadrant $C$: the product retraction $c \times r$, with retract $\{(1, 0)\} \times r(U)$, is not tame. At $((0, 0), u)$, $u \in r(U)$, the degeneracy index is $1 + d_C(u)$, at its image $((1, 0), u)$ it is $d_C(u)$.

(b) If $(f, y)$, $f(y) = 0$, is in good position in some chart and has tame germ data, it is in good position in that tame chart.

V4.1

Definition 4.1: corner charts and corner structures

restated
compatibility = equivalence of atlasesdimension may vary

HWZ §4.1, Definition 4.1, p. 147

An M-polyfold $X$ has a compatible smooth manifold structure with boundary with corners if it admits an atlas of sc-smoothly compatible charts $(V, \varphi, (U, C, \mathbb R^n))$, $\varphi : V \to U$ an sc-diffeomorphism from an open $V \subseteq X$ onto a relatively open subset $U$ of a partial quadrant $C$ in $\mathbb R^n$ (or in a finite-dimensional vector space).

Proved in Lean

A corner chart (MChart.IsCornerChart) is a chart whose model is $(U, C, V)$ with $V$ finite-dimensional, the constant sc-structure, $U$ relatively open in the partial quadrant $C$, and the identity retraction. HasCornerStructure: an atlas of corner charts equivalent to the atlas of $X$; equivalently every point lies in a corner chart that is a chart of $X$. The dimension may vary. Corner models are tame retracts and sc⁺-retracts; a corner structure makes $X$ tame.

If $X_0 = X_\infty$, $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ has the inverse $1_1^0$, which is always sc-smooth; so if $1_0^1$ is sc-smooth it is an sc-diffeomorphism. For a finite-dimensional $V$: $(\mathrm{const}\,V)^1 = \mathrm{const}\,V$, the lift is the identity, every retract is an sc⁺-retract. The example (remark_4_3_example): an M-polyfold with $X_0 = X_\infty$ for which $1_0^1 : X \to X^1$ is not sc-smooth, so $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds; it is a retract $O = O_\infty \subseteq \mathbb R \oplus X$ that is not an sc⁺-retract (remark_4_3_retract_example), the image of the retraction $(t, z) \mapsto (t, L(t)z)$ of moving rank-one projections on a weighted sequence space, sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss (IsLossFamily.isScSmooth). $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ as sets (MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff).

  • “It is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as M-polyfolds although the sets agree” is proved by an example the text does not give (fourth addendum of this page; formerly gap G.31). By Proposition 4.8 an example is a retract $O = O_\infty$ that is not an sc⁺-retract; it cannot come from a retraction whose level maps are $C^1$ (an argument, not formalized), so its retraction loses a level in its first derivative, as the splicings of HWZ do, and its sc-smoothness rests on a criterion with loss proved for it, not on Proposition 1.19.   • “$X^1 \ne X$” is read as “$1_0^1$ is not sc-smooth”, equivalently (by remark_4_3_isScDiffeo) “the identity is not an sc-diffeomorphism $X \to X^1$”. The sc-diffeomorphism clause needs only $X = X_1$, not $X_0 = X_\infty$. “$(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$” misprints $X_0$; $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ holds as sets, the topologies of the iterated levels being gap G.6 (Findings, Chapter 4, items 5, 125). Hence “stronger” (formerly “narrower”, for the missing example).

Theorem 4.23: families and Sard's theorem

stronger
stratified regular valuescountable cover$A_\lambda$ also tame

HWZ §4.3, Theorem 4.23, p. 165 (proof pp. 165–166)

Let $A \subseteq Z$ be a smooth submanifold with tame induced structure and compact closure, $p = P|_A$, $\varepsilon > 0$ with (1) $p^{-1}(\lambda)$ compact and non-empty for $|\lambda| \le \varepsilon$, (2) "for $z \in A$ there exists a sc-complement $T_zA$ in $T_zZ$ contained in $T^R_zZ$". Then there is $\Sigma \subseteq \{|\lambda| < \varepsilon\}$ of full measure of regular values of $p$ such that for $\lambda \in \Sigma$, $A_\lambda$ is a smooth compact manifold with boundary with corners in general position.

Proved in Lean

With (2) read as general position at every point: there is $\Sigma \subseteq \{|\lambda| < \varepsilon\}$ with Lebesgue-null complement, of stratified regular values, such that each $A_\lambda$, $\lambda \in \Sigma$, is compact, a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of $X$ in general position, with a corner structure, tame.

By Proposition 2.36 the codimension of $T^R_xX$ is $d_X(x)$; so for $\lambda \in \Sigma$ a point of $A_\lambda$ can lie in a corner only if $d_X(x) \le \dim A_\lambda$; zero-dimensional $A_\lambda$ lie in $X \setminus \partial X$.

What differs

  • $Y^i \to X^i$ is never defined in the text (it defines $Y[i]$ for $i = 0, 1$). $Y^1$ is read as $Y_{1,1}$ with $(Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}$, the convention of $E^1$ and of $(U \triangleleft F)^1 = U^1 \triangleleft F^1$; it is forced by “$f^i$ is obtained by raising the index”: an sc-smooth section maps $X_1$ into $Y_{1,1}$, in general not into $Y_{1,2}$. The fibre of $P^1$ carries the topology of $F_1$, not that of the fibre of $P$; it is a Banach space because a fibre of a strong bundle is, through a chart, a closed subspace of its fibre model (StrongBundleChart.isBanachable_fiber) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 140, 141).
  • “It is a priori clear” hides condition (3) of the filling on level $1$ ($\ker Dr^1(0) \to \ker\rho^1(0)$ a topological isomorphism), which does not follow from level $0$ alone: an sc-operator can be bijective on level $0$ and not onto on level $1$. It holds for the data of Definition 3.11: subtracting the section $z \mapsto \Gamma(z, -g(0))$ reduces to $g(0) = 0$ with the same fill defect (Lemma 3.17), Proposition 3.52 in sc form makes $Dg(0)$ sc-Fredholm, and its regularity gives the surjectivity on level $1$; the open mapping theorem does the rest (Findings, Chapter 5, items 22, 144). No hypothesis beyond the text’s is added.
  • Tameness is not used. The tame form (germ data of $f^1$ in tame charts of $P^1$) is not stated: the tameness of the index raise of a tame chart is not proved, and no counterexample is known (Findings, Chapter 5, item 145). $i \ge 2$ by iteration: V5.13. Hence “stronger”: the strong bundle need not be tame, as in V5.10, and the round-trip audit confirms A ⇒ B, not B ⇒ A (refreshed 2026-11-02; “same” in the fourth addendum, “narrower” before it: no $Y^1 \to X^1$, no filler on level $1$) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 140–146; gap G.41).
  • In the text’s germ reading of Definition 3.11 (phase 2) $s^1$ is an sc⁺-germ on the shifted germ of $s$, and the level-$1$ conjugation uses $g - s$ only near $0$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 333).

HasBumpAt: $x$ is a bump point if every open $U \ni x$ carries an sc-smooth $f$ with $f(x) \ne 0$ and $\operatorname{supp} f \subseteq U$; the pointwise reading is “every point is a bump point”, and the weak reading follows from “the bump points are dense” (admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_of_dense). On an sc-Banach space the weak reading gives a bump point at every smooth point (AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth); on M-polyfolds built on sc-Hilbert spaces the pointwise reading holds (admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert).

What differs

  • The text’s “$(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ is not complete” is false without a hypothesis: for $U = \emptyset$ the space is a point, and over a point with finite-dimensional fibre it is the closed unit ball of $\mathbb R^k$. It is read as “not complete in general” and proved by an example: the allowable sections $s_j(x) = (x, \sqrt{x^2 + 1/(j+1)^2}/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2}))$ form a $\rho$-Cauchy sequence whose pointwise limit has fibre part $|x|/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2})$, not differentiable at $0$, while the fibre part of an sc⁺-section of the trivial bundle is $C^1$. That non-completeness holds whenever $U$ contains a non-isolated point over which $Y_{0,1}$ is nonzero (the text’s setting) is expected by the same mechanism and not formalized (Findings, Chapter 5, items 150–153; gap G.42).
  • Only Definition 5.1 (1) is used for the metric axioms (symmetry and subadditivity of the fibre norms, $N$ vanishing only at $0_x$); the density statements of Theorems 5.13 and 5.18 are $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$ (allowableDist_le_iff; V5.30, V5.39). Hence still “restated”; before the fourth addendum of this page $\rho$ was used pointwise only and the metric space was not formalized (Findings, Chapter 5, item 47).

G.1

Example 1.2: the weighted Sobolev spaces $H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$

not formalized

HWZ §1.1, Example 1.2, pp. 6–7

With $0 = \delta_0 < \delta_1 < \cdots$, the spaces $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$ of $L^2$ functions whose weak derivatives up to order $m$, weighted by $e^{\delta_m|s|}$, are in $L^2$ form an sc-structure on $L^2(\mathbb R \times S^1)$, "using Sobolev's compact embedding theorem for bounded domains and the assumption that $(\delta_m)$ is strictly increasing".

In the formalization

Not formalized. Mathlib has no weighted Sobolev spaces and no Rellich–Kondrachov theorem; the exposition proves the example in full (Proposition 1.C). The only examples of sc-Banach spaces built here are the constant structure on a finite-dimensional space, and the sums, shifts, sc-subspaces and quotients of sc-Banach spaces (V1.1, V1.4, V1.6). This example, with the shift map of the 2010 paper, is the project's planned step H2.

G.3

Definition 1.14: $Df$ need not be norm continuous

formalized since
now V1.13now V1.34

HWZ §1.1, after Definition 1.14, p. 11

"In general, the map $U_1 \to \mathcal L(E_0, F_0)$, defined by $x \mapsto Df(x)$, will not(!) be continuous, if the space of bounded linear operators is equipped with the operator norm."

In the formalization

Formalized since the first edition of this page (third addendum; V1.13, V1.34), by an example (the text gives none). $X$ is the sc-Banach space of sequences whose level $m$ consists of the $x$ with $(k+1)^m x_k \to 0$, normed by $|x|_m = \sup_k (k+1)^m|x_k|$: every level is a copy of $c_0$, the inclusion $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ is $\mathrm{diag}(1/(k+1))$, compact, and the finitely supported sequences are smooth points dense in every level. On $E = \mathbb R \oplus X$ the map $f(t, x)_k = \cos(kt)x_k$ is $\mathrm{sc}^1$ with $Df(t, x)(\tau, \xi)_k = -k\sin(kt)x_k\tau + \cos(kt)\xi_k$ (the factor $k$ is absorbed by one level). $(\pi/(n+1), 0) \to 0$ in $E_1$, but $\|Df(\pi/(n+1), 0) - Df(0, 0)\| \ge 2$ (test on the unit vector $e_{n+1}$); since the derivative is unique on $E_1$, no derivative family of $f$ is continuous for the operator norm. Not formalized: that $f$ is sc-smooth (it is), and the shift map of the exposition (§6), which needs Example 1.2 (G.1).

Proposition 2.2: classical smooth retractions have submanifold images

not formalized

HWZ §2.1, Proposition 2.2, p. 18 (proof §2.6.1, pp. 54–55)

If $r : U \to U$ is a $C^\infty$ retraction of an open subset of a Banach space $E$, then $O = r(U)$ is a $C^\infty$ submanifold: near each $x \in O$ there are a splitting $E = R \oplus N$ and a diffeomorphism $\psi : V \to W$ with $\psi(O \cap V) = R \cap W$ (the text prints $\psi(0) = x$ for $\psi(x) = 0$).

In the formalization

Not formalized. The proposition is classical and is used only as motivation (the contrast with sc-smooth retractions, whose images can change dimension). The exposition proves it in §8.1 with the inverse function theorem; its Lean version would need Mathlib's inverse function theorem for $C^\infty$ maps between Banach spaces and the splitting by the projection $Dr(0)$. Not attempted.

Theorem 3.23 and Corollary 3.24: implicit function theorem, boundary case

formalized since
now V3.69now V3.70now V3.95now V3.97

HWZ §3.1, Theorem 3.23 and Corollary 3.24, pp. 77–78

At a zero with surjective linearization whose kernel is in good position to $C_xX$, the local solution set consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold with a unique structure of a manifold with boundary with corners; globally if this holds at every zero.

In the formalization

Formalized since the first edition of this page. Theorem 3.23 (V3.69): the local solution set consists of smooth points and is a tame sub-M-polyfold equivalent to a $d$-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners, when $x$ and the zeros near it are in good position in tame charts (V3.103; or under the filler condition at the nearby zeros, V3.82), and since the second addendum with the text's hypotheses (V3.95), with the dimension as the Fredholm index (V3.97). Corollary 3.24 (V3.70) with the text's hypotheses: good position in a tame chart at every zero gives a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure, a manifold with boundary with corners of locally constant dimension.

Theorem 3.54 (1) with the text's hypotheses: surjectivity of $f'(y)$ at the nearby zeros

formalized since
now V3.81now V3.82now V3.93now V3.94

HWZ §3.6, Theorem 3.54 (1), pp. 111–114

(1) At every zero $y$ near $x$ the germ $(f, y)$ is in good position, “from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55”; (2) the solution set near $x$ is a sub-M-polyfold with the structure of a manifold with boundary with corners.

In the formalization

Formalized since the first edition of this page (V3.93, V3.94): with the text's hypotheses (tame germ data, good position in a tame chart, V3.103), every zero $y$ near $x_0$ is in good position in a tame chart, in particular $f'(y)$ is onto. The text's argument does not give the surjectivity (it gives that of the filled linearization only; the same step is in the book's arXiv version); it is proved by an implicit function theorem at the nearby zero for $g + \mu\rho(r(\cdot))\lambda$, with Theorem 3.30 at the centre for a contraction germ whose regions in $a$ do not depend on $\lambda$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 180–189). The first form under the filler condition at the nearby zeros (V3.82) is kept; that condition follows from good position (V3.102). (2) is proved from (1) (V3.85, V3.94); the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98).

Theorem 3.19: the dimension is the index; $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$; good position for $d_X \equiv 0$

formalized since
now V3.97now V3.98now V3.99now V3.100now V3.101

HWZ §3.1, Theorem 3.19, p. 74

The solution set near $x_0$ is a manifold whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index of $f'(x_0)$; at its points $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$; and for $d_X(x) = 0$ good position is the surjectivity of $f'(x)$.

In the formalization

Formalized since the first edition of this page (second addendum). The dimension: the dimension $d$ of the solution set near a zero in good position is $\dim\ker f'(y) = \mathrm{ind}\,f'(y)$ at every zero $y$ near it, in every chart (V3.97, with V3.96), also in Theorems 3.23, 3.57, and the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98). The kernel: $D\psi$ maps $\ker f'(y)$, read in the chart at $x_0$, onto the tangent space of the solution graph (V3.99); $T_yS$ as a subspace of $T_yX$ is not formalized (Chapter 2 gap G.13). Good position in a tame chart at $d_X(y) = 0$ is surjectivity, for tame germ data (V3.100), so Theorems 3.19 and 3.56 hold with “$f'(x)$ surjective” (V3.101).

Remark 4.3: “$X^1 \ne X$ is possible”

formalized since
now V4.6

HWZ §4.1, Remark 4.3, p. 148

If $X_0 = X_\infty$, then $X_m = X_0$ as sets for all $m$; "however, it is possible that $X^1 \ne X$ as sc-smooth spaces despite the fact that $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1} = X_i$ as sets".

In the formalization

Formalized since the first edition of this page (fourth addendum; V4.6), by an example the text does not give. On the weighted sequence space $X$ of V1.13 ($|x|_m = \sup_k(k+1)^m|x_k|$), $L(t)$ is the projection onto $\cos\theta\,e_{n_k} + \sin\theta\,e_{n_{k+1}}$ ($n_k = 2^k$), the angle $\theta$ turning from $0$ to $\pi/2$ with flat ends while $t$ runs through $[1/(k+2), 1/(k+1)]$, and $L(t) = 0$ for $t \le 0$. The retraction $r(t, z) = (t, L(t)z)$ of $\mathbb R \oplus X$ is sc-smooth by a criterion for parameter families of level operators with one level of loss; its retract $O$ consists of smooth points, and the lift $O \to E_1$ is discontinuous at $0$, so $O$ is not an sc⁺-retract (Proposition 4.8), and the M-polyfold $O$ with its single chart has $X_0 = X_\infty$ and $1_0^1$ not sc-smooth. Why an example needs a retraction that loses a level (one with $C^1$ level maps gives none) is an argument, not formalized (Findings, Chapter 4, items 140–146).

$\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ "becomes a metric space with respect to the uniform distance $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$. The metric space $(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ is not complete."
